name: Cherry tomatoes
tile_uses: Pasta, the sheet pan, rice bowls
why_now: Cherry tomatoes are still running strong in August and can be exceptional — concentrated flavor, thin skins that burst easily. Where July favored big heirlooms for slicing and eating raw, August is when cherry tomatoes hit their stride, especially the sungold and mixed varieties.
how_to_choose: Firm but not hard — should give slightly when pressed
Deep, even color throughout (red, orange, or yellow depending on variety)
Avoid any with wrinkled skins or soft spots
buy_this_much: 1 pint for the week — they'll appear in pasta, tacos, and rice bowls, and disappear faster than expected.
price_note: Cherry tomatoes are widely available in August at most grocery stores and farmers markets. Mixed varieties at farmers markets often include sungolds and grape tomatoes, which are worth seeking out.

flavor_paths.name: Burst in oil
flavor_paths.description: In a hot pan until they split. The fresh flavor, and the pasta sauce.

flavor_paths.name: Roasted
flavor_paths.description: On the sheet pan until slumped and sweet.

flavor_paths.name: Raw
flavor_paths.description: Halved. Their acidity does the seasoning.

weekday_uses: Burst in olive oil for pasta
weekend_use: A handful burst in the pork pan after the nectarines, if you want more sauce.
storage: Counter at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. Do not refrigerate — cold ruins the texture and flavor. Use within three or four days.
one_thing_to_learn: Bursting cherry tomatoes in a hot pan is one of the most reliable weekday techniques. The key is patience — add them to a hot pan with olive oil, don't stir, and let them blister and split on their own. The skin will tighten, then burst, releasing liquid that becomes the sauce. Stir once they've started to collapse. Add garlic and basil after the heat is off.
market_question: Do you have sungolds? What's the sweetest variety this week?
